title: Tile-based progressive response sandbox
content:
Problem / context:
- Many client surfaces want earlier partial results (fast first content) while progressively adding detail. Current streaming is token-level which is hard to reason about for UX and cost budgeting.
- Some apps prefer a coarse answer quickly and optional deeper tiles (explain, citations, expanded examples).
- We can trade latency/cost/quality by splitting an output into discrete "tiles" with independently configurable fidelity and routing.

Idea (high level):
- Represent a model response as an ordered list of tiles. Each tile is a self-contained chunk (summary, key facts, example, code snippet, citations).
- Client can request only the first N tiles (fast path) or stream tiles as they complete. Tiles can be served by different model variants / quantization / backends (small fast model -> summary tile; larger model -> deep explanation tile).
- Backend exposes a simple contract: tile schema + manifest for the response. The manifest is tiny and streams immediately; tiles follow.

Why tiles vs tokens:
- Predictable UX: clients render tile containers, fill when tile arrives.
- Easier caching and reuse: summary tiles cacheable across similar prompts; deep tiles can be cached separately.
- Routing and cost control: route expensive tiles to Dedicated pools or delay them.
- User-level controls: allow user to opt into deeper tiles (consent to longer latency / cost).

Example user stories:
- As a mobile user, I want a crisp one-sentence answer instantly, with an option to expand into examples if needed.
- As a docs writer, I want a quick outline and then an optional deep-dive block that includes citations and expanded examples.
- As a platform engineer, I want to route the deep tiles to Dedicated GPUs and keep the summary tile on cheap hosted tiers.

Tile manifest sketch (API):
- Client POST /responses with prompt + tile_spec (requested tiles or preference).
- Response 200: { manifest: [ {id, type, estimated_size_tokens, estimated_latency_ms, model_hint}], early_tiles: [tile1?] } (manifest streams immediately)
- Subsequent: SSE/WebSocket/HTTP2 pushes tile blobs as they complete.

Tile types (initial list):
- summary (1-2 sentences)
- quick-facts (bullet list)
- example (short code / usage example)
- reasoning (step-by-step explanation)
- citations (sources + snippets)
- expansion (long-form paragraph)

Routing & fidelity strategy:
- summary -> cheapest fast model (quantized, CPU/GPU small) with aggressive temperature tuning
- quick-facts -> medium model
- reasoning/expansion -> larger high-accuracy model (optionally Dedicated)
- citations -> model + retrieval pipeline; can be produced after retrieval pass
- fallback policy: if deep tile fails or times out, serve a short apology tile + link to summary

Cost model (rough):
- Cost per tile = base invocation cost + per-token cost for that tile's model.
- Billing: either bundle manifest + tiles into single response invoice or itemize per tile so clients can select only charged tiles.
- Experiment: allow "pay-as-you-expand" where initial request charged for manifest+first tile, additional tiles billed when fetched.

UX notes / client contract ideas:
- Render placeholders for each declared tile immediately (from manifest).
- Include tile state: pending, streaming, complete, failed.
- Provide an "expand" API for clients to request next/high-fidelity tiles on demand.
- Consider backwards compatibility: if client doesn't support tiles, return flattened streaming text combining tiles.

Open questions / risks:
- How to define tile boundaries reliably from model outputs (we need model scaffolding to produce tile-delimited outputs).
- Consistency: generation with multiple models (summary by small model, details by big model) may disagree. Need reconciliation rules.
- Latency: manifest still an extra round-trip; need manifest to be extremely cheap to produce.
- Caching semantics and cache invalidation for tiles tied to prompt variants.
- Billing complexity and UX for customers.

Experiment plan (MVP):
1) Internal prototype (2 weeks): implement server-side manifest generator + tile runner. Use a small set of templates to force tile boundaries (e.g., prefix: "---TILE:summary---").
2) Client demo (1 week): minimal web demo that requests only summary+example tiles and allows expansion.
3) A/B test (4 weeks): route 10% of support-bot traffic through tile pipeline to measure latency, conversion (did users expand?), retention of expanded tile users.
4) Cost analysis: compare token cost vs perceived UX improvements; estimate break-even for pay-as-you-expand billing.

Success metrics (initial):
- Time-to-first-tile median under 300ms for summary tiles on hosted tier.
- Expand rate: % of sessions that request >=2 tiles (proxy for user engagement with deeper content).
- Accuracy regression: deep tile answers should not contradict summary > 1% of sampled queries (define detection heuristic).
- Cost per session delta: no more than +30% for sessions where users do not expand.

Implementation notes / quick sketches:
- Prompt scaffolding: use deterministic separators and tile labels to coax model into tile outputs. e.g. "<TILE:summary>...<END>"
- Orchestration: manifest created by a lightweight planner service that maps requested tile types to model variants & queues tile jobs.
- Streaming: use existing streaming infra with a small manifest event first, then attach tile streams as child events.
- Tracing: annotate trace with tile ids, model variant, latency, token count. Important for Optimize tooling and RL monitoring.

Next actions (today):
- [ ] Sync with Maya on UX placeholder semantics and error states. (Maya)
- [ ] Ask infra if we can cheaply spin up small model variant for summary (Kai)
- [ ] Draft a tiny demo prompt set (50 prompts across faq/support/docs) we can use for A/B (me)
- [ ] File INF-7242 as umbrella ticket and assign initial spike PR (Evan)

Notes to self / heuristics:
- Start with small discrete tile set (summary, example, citation) before adding reasoning tiles.
- Keep manifest tiny: clients should render without waiting for tile generation.
- Favor "pull" model for expensive tiles to reduce wasted computation (generate only when requested).

Slack crumbs / references:
- saw earlier convo with @maya on tile placeholders (link in Confluence).
- related: INF-5981 (prefetching session proxies) might intersect — don't duplicate logic.

Rough sample prompt + expected manifest (toy):
User prompt: "How to set up S3 backup for our Redwood DB?"
Manifest (fast): [ {id: "t1", type: "summary", est_tokens: 20}, {id: "t2", type: "steps", est_tokens: 120}, {id: "t3", type: "example", est_tokens: 60}, {id: "t4", type: "citations", est_tokens: 40} ]
First tile (t1) quick: "Use Redwood DB snapshot exports + an S3 lifecycle; steps: snapshot -> export -> verify."
If user clicks expand, request tile t2 (steps) which is routed to a medium model.

Backlog ideas (nice-to-have):
- Tile-level QoS and SLA (dedicated for critical tiles)
- Per-tile semantic versioning for cached tiles (so clients can invalidate outdated expansions)
- Tile composition editor in Console (product folks can design default tile ordering per route)

Ending note: this feels like a promising tradeoff space between streaming and discrete micro-documents. Need to validate if users actually prefer explicit tiles vs token stream. MVP should be small and easy to adopt (compat back to streaming).
